description: Pins the Myne dialect task-field extension (dialect/src/lezer/task-field.ts + taskFields.ts + taskFieldWriter.ts) across all THREE read dialects and the ONE emitted form. Each case carries the recognized spans (UTF-8 byte offsets, pre-order), the typed record, and the line as Myne would write it. Emoji markers are surrogate pairs in UTF-16 and four bytes in UTF-8, so the byte-offset convention is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. `inert` cases are near-misses the recognizer must NOT claim. TS-runner category (no Rust generator).

cases.description: A due date in Obsidian's Dataview-style inline-field form.
A recurrence rule in the Dataview form.
Obsidian's `completion` key folds onto Myne's `done` — the whole of the third dialect a reader must learn.
A reminder carrying a wall-clock time, with no offset and no zone id.
A priority in its word form.
All five typed fields on one line; emission reorders them into the stable order.

cases.description: A half-written date does not type; it is preserved rather than completed.
A date that passes the shape but does not exist is refused, never corrected.
An out-of-range hour is refused.
A Z offset does not type at all — stripping it would silently shift the due date.
A numeric offset is refused for the same reason, and keeps a coarse geolocation datum out of an exported plaintext file.
A priority word outside the five levels is preserved, not approximated.
A field inside a code span is not a field — inline parsing never runs inside a range the code node has consumed.
An ordinary markdown link and a dangling label are not fields, even though the bracketed rule outranks Link.
